subject: zoology
question_text: Distinguish between hypertrophy and hyperplasia with an example for each.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.44, SAQ 46). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Hypertrophy
lines: Hypertrophy: some parasites cause an abnormal
increase in the SIZE of the host cell. The cell
The number of cells does not change; each cell
Example: Plasmodium inside a red blood cell
makes the cell grow to almost double its normal
size, and the cell finally bursts.
steps.why: Hypertrophy is a change in size only, so the answer states that the cell number stays the same — that single line is what separates it from hyperplasia.
common_mistakes: Writing that the number of cells increases. That is hyperplasia.
Giving Fasciola as the example. Fasciola is the hyperplasia example.
steps.memory_tip: Trophy means growth of one cell: hypertrophy is a bigger cell, same number.
steps.margin_note: Definition, the size-not-number line, then the example. Two marks, so give all three.

steps.label: Hyperplasia
lines: Hyperplasia: some parasites cause an increase in
the size of an organ by increasing the NUMBER of
its cells. This causes inconvenience or death to
Example: Fasciola hepatica lives in the bile
ducts of sheep. It increases the number of cells
of the duct wall, and the thickened wall blocks
steps.why: Hyperplasia is a change in number, and the harm comes from the extra cells thickening a wall and blocking a passage, which is why the bile duct is the example that is set.
common_mistakes: Writing that the cells become larger. In hyperplasia they become more numerous.
Naming Fasciola without saying what is blocked. The blocked bile duct is the harm.
steps.memory_tip: Plasia means forming: hyperplasia is more cells, hypertrophy is bigger cells.
steps.margin_note: Definition, then the example with the blocked duct. Two marks.

insider_note: A 'distinguish' question is marked on the contrast, so use the words SIZE and NUMBER plainly in the two halves.
